If the edge of a cube is increased by 2 cm, the volume will increase by 488 cm³. What then will be the length of each edge of the cube?

⇒ (x + 2)³ – x³ = 488

⇒ x³ + 6x² + 12x + 8 – x³ = 488

⇒ 6x² + 12x – 480 = 0

⇒ x² + 2x – 80 = 0

⇒ (x – 8) (x + 10) = 0

⇒ x = 8, -10

⇒ x = 8 cm

questions.question: If the 8 digit number 136p5785 is divisible by 15, then find the least possible value of P.

Factors of 15 = (3 × 5) and the divisibility rule of 15 says that sum of digits be divided by 3 and the last number will be 5.

The given number is = 136p5785, here the last digit is 5, so we will check divisibility of 3.

⇒ 1 + 3 + 6 + p + 5 + 7 + 8 + 5 = 35 + p

The closed multiple of 3 is 36

⇒ 36 = 35 + p

∴ p = 36 – 35= 1

questions.question: How many atoms will one mole of Carbon (C – 12) contain?
questions.solution:
__Concept__:

Avogadro's number: The number of units present in one mole of a given substance is called the Avogadro's number.

__
 
• Avogadro's number (NA) is equal to 6.022140857 × 1023.
 
• This number also called Avogadro's constant is equal to the number of atoms present in 12 grams of Carbon-12.
 
• Mole is a fundamental unit of measure of the amount of a substance.
 
• For atoms, the mass of Avogadro's number of particles is equal to their atomic mass in grams.
 
• For molecules, the mass of Avogadro's number of particles is equal to their molecular mass in grams.

Explanation__:

__
 
• A mole is a unit of measurement which is defined as a quantity of anything which has the same number of particles (atoms, molecules, etc) as are found in 12 grams of carbon-12.
 
• The number of particles is defined as Avogadro’s Number and it is approximately 6.02×1023.

That is, 1 mole of carbon has 6.02×1023 atoms of carbon and weighs 12 grams.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• C-12 is an isotope of Carbon and is widely used as a standard for **measurement of atomic masses of all nuclides.**

questions.question: A train, starting from rest, attains a velocity of 90 km/h in 5 minutes. Assuming that the acceleration is uniform, the distance travelled by the train during this time is:
questions.solution:
**Initial Velocity** = u = 0 km/h

**Final velocity** = v = 90 km/h

**Time** = 5 min = 5/60 h = 1/12 h

Acceleration = a = ?

**a** = (v-u)/t

a = (90-0)/ (1/12)

= 90 ×12

**__= 1080 km/h²__**

**Distance travelled = s = ut+ (1/2) at²**

= 0x (1/12) + (1/2) × (1080) × (1/12)²

= (1/2) x1080x (1/144)

= 3.75km

**__∴ Distance travelled by the train = 3.75km.__**

questions.question: If a + 1/a = 3, then a³ + 1/a³ = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If a + 1/a = k, then a³ + 1/a³ = k³ − 3k

Given, k = 3.

a³ + 1/a³ = 3³ − 3 × 3

⇒ 27 − 9 = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

a + 1/a = 3

**Formula Used:**

(x + y)³ = x³ + y³ + 3xy(x + y)

**Calculations:**

Substitute x = a and y = 1/a into the algebraic identity:

⇒ (a + 1/a)³ = a³ + 1/a³ + 3 × a × (1/a) × (a + 1/a)

⇒ (a + 1/a)³ = a³ + 1/a³ + 3 × (a + 1/a)

Substitute the given value a + 1/a = 3 into the equation:

⇒ 3³ = a³ + 1/a³ + 3 × 3

⇒ 27 = a³ + 1/a³ + 9

⇒ a³ + 1/a³ = 27 − 9

⇒ a³ + 1/a³ = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Minus Identity for Cubes

If x − 1/x = k, then x³ − 1/x³ = k³ + 3k.

Square Identity (Plus)

If x + 1/x = k, then x² + 1/x² = k² − 2.

Square Identity (Minus)

If x − 1/x = k, then x² + 1/x² = k² + 2.

Fourth Power Identity

If x + 1/x = k, then x⁴ + 1/x⁴ = (k² − 2)² − 2.

questions.question: To go a certain distance of 40 km upstream a rower takes 8 hours while it takes her only 5 hours to row the same distance downstream. What was the rower’s speed in still water?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Downstream speed = 40 ÷ 5 = 8 km/h

Upstream speed = 40 ÷ 8 = 5 km/h

Speed in still water = (Downstream speed + Upstream speed) ÷ 2

⇒ (8 + 5) ÷ 2 = 6.5 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 6.5 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance covered upstream and downstream (d) = 40 km

Time taken upstream (tᵤ) = 8 hours

Time taken downstream (td) = 5 hours

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Speed in still water = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 

 
 

 
 

 

 Downstream (With stream)
 Distance = 40 km, Time = 5 h → Speed = 8 km/h
 
 Upstream (Against stream)
 Distance = 40 km, Time = 8 h → Speed = 5 km/h
 
 Speed in still water = (8 + 5) ÷ 2 = 6.5 km/h

**Calculations:**

⇒ Downstream Speed (Sd) = 40 ÷ 5 = 8 km/h

⇒ Upstream Speed (Sᵤ) = 40 ÷ 8 = 5 km/h

⇒ Speed in still water = (Sd + Sᵤ) ÷ 2

⇒ Speed in still water = (8 + 5) ÷ 2

⇒ Speed in still water = 13 ÷ 2 = 6.5 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 6.5 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed Downstream (Sd)

It is the speed of the boat when travelling in the same direction as the stream. Formula: Sd = Speed of boat in still water + Speed of stream.

Speed Upstream (Sᵤ)

It is the speed of the boat when travelling against the direction of the stream. Formula: Sᵤ = Speed of boat in still water − Speed of stream.

Speed of Stream

The velocity of the current or river can be calculated directly if downstream and upstream speeds are known using the formula: Speed of stream = (Sd − Sᵤ) ÷ 2.
</p

questions.question:
Consider the given question and decide which of the following statement is sufficient to answer the question.

What are the values of p, q and r?

**Statements:**

1. (p + q)² = 16

2. p – q = 4; r = 2p

options.text: Neither 1 nor 2 is sufficient to answer the question.
Only 1 is sufficient to answer the question
Only 2 is sufficient to answer the question
Both 1 and 2 together are sufficient to answer the question.

questions.solution:
From statement 1,

(p + q)² = 16

⇒ p + q = ± 4

Now from statement 2,

p – q = 4, r = 2p

From 1 and 2 we can get an answer

p + q = 4 (Equation 1)

were p = 4+q (Equation 2)

4+q+q = 4 **(solving)**

2q = 0, (**q=0)**

p + q = 4

**(p = 4)**

**r = 2 × p = 2 × 4 = 8**

Combining both statements we can get a fixed value of **p = 4, q = 0, and r =8.**

∴ Both 1 and 2 together are sufficient to answer the question.

questions.question:
Solve the following

7 × {4 + (-2) × (-3)} = ?
Find the compound interest on Rs. 62500 at 21% per annum for 1(1)/(2) years compounded half yearly.
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

Principle(P) = Rs. 62500

Rate of interest(r) = 21% per annum = 10.5% half yearly

Time(n) = 3/2 years = 3 half years

**FORMULA USED:**

A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

Where,

A= Amount, P = Principle ,r = Rate of interest , n = Time 

**CALCULATION:**

⇒ A = 62500(1 + 10.5/100)³

⇒ A = 62500 × (110.5/100)³

⇒ A = 62500 × 110.5/100 × 110.5/100 × 110.5/100

⇒ A = Rs. 84327.03

∴ Compound Interest earned = A – P= 84327.03 – 62500 = Rs. 21827.03

11 + 6 = 17,

So, 17 + 8 = 25

questions.question: There was a group of six student who took a test. Another student joined the group after taking the test later. With her marks included the average score of the group went up by 3. This student has got _________ marks more than the average marks without her being included.
questions.solution:
Let the average be ‘x’.

x = Total marks/Total no. of students

⇒ Total marks = 6 × x ----(1)

Now including a girl, average increased by 3

⇒ (x + 3) = Total marks/7

⇒ Total marks = 7(x × 3) = 7x + 21

⇒ Increased marks = 7x + 21 – 6x = x + 21

∴ The girl got 21 marks more than the average marks without her being included.

questions.question: Praneet started his journey at 2:45:46 p.m. and reached the destination at 4:55:57 p.m. Anit started the journey 58 mins 40 secs after Praneet and reached his destination 50 mins 29 secs after him. How long did Anit take to complete his journey?
questions.solution:
Anit’s time when he starts his journey = Praneet’s starting time + 0:58:40

⇒ Anit’s time = 2:45:46 + 0:58:40 = 3:44:26 pm

Anit’s reaching time = Praneet’ reaching time + 0:50:29

⇒ Anit’s reaching time = 4:55:57 + 0:50:29 = 5:46:26 pm

∴ Time taken by Anit in journey = 5:46:26 – 3:44:26= 2:02:00 hrs= 2 hours 2 mins
